conditionalAwardEvidence.formulaText: For a selected Alaska NEVI project, the federal NEVI share may not exceed 80% of eligible project costs; private or state funds may provide the non-federal share. Runtime conditional award should be calculated only after a current RFA/selection/project agreement or award notice is known: min(approved_award_amount_cents, round(eligible_project_cost_cents * 0.80)), with non_federal_match_cents at least 20% of eligible cost and all NEVI/Title 23/Buy America/public-access requirements satisfied. FHWA guidance confirms the 80% federal cost-share ceiling and non-federal share structure; AEA's FY26 plan says project agreements include reimbursement/billing methods, NEPA, Title 23, Buy America, property interest, Uniform Act, Clean Air Act, and milestone reimbursement terms. ([Federal Highway Administration][1])
conditionalAwardEvidence.notes: The 80% figure is a maximum federal cost-share, not a guaranteed award. A current Alaska NEVI solicitation, selected/approved application status, eligible cost basis, approved award amount, non-federal match, NEVI-compliant public EV charging scope, and reimbursement timing must be confirmed before any conditional award is calculable. The active AIDEA/AEA procurement page checked on 2026-07-04 did not show an active NEVI RFA; it showed only an AIDEA hangar RFI. ([AIDEA/AEA Procurement][2])

The Joint Office separately reported the same nine-community and $6.4 million conditional-award summary. ([AWS][4])

awardHistory.evidenceText: The NASEO/AASHTO/Atlas case study reports 34 proposals from eight applicants across 13 of 14 priority areas and nine prospective awards submitted by four entities across nine priority locations. Its award table lists four Tesla awards of $490,907, three eCAMION USA awards of $875,951, one North Anchorage Real Estate Investors award of $1,039,746, and one Browman Development Company Wasilla award of $952,950; RetroFi-computed line-item total is $6,584,177, with average $731,575.22, median $875,951, minimum $490,907, and maximum $1,039,746. probabilityRecommendation.notes: A historical application-to-site-award ratio is derivable for the 2023 Phase 1 corridor RFA: 9 site/community awards divided by 34 applications equals 26.47%. However, no official current-round applicant count, expected award count, open RFA, or current Phase 2 scoring/budget package was found. The 2023 numerator is site/community/prospective-award based and the denominator is application/proposal based; NASEO also reports eight distinct applicants and four distinct awardee entities. Because Phase 2 is expected to differ from Phase 1 and AEA's FY26 plan notes Tesla proceeding with four previously awarded sites without NEVI funding, RetroFi should not automatically use the historical ratio as a current project probability. ([AK Energy Authority][5])

fallbackPriorSuggestion.basis: Human-review-only historical anchor: 9 first-round Phase 1 AFC site/community awards divided by 34 applications equals 26.47%. This should be considered only if a current Alaska NEVI solicitation is confirmed to be materially comparable to the 2023 RFA in applicant pool, site-count structure, eligible project type, scoring, and available funding. It is not suitable for automatic expected-value estimates from eligibility alone.
